title: Get started with dlmoR
text: calculate_dlmo() returns ordinary R objects, dlmoR fits easily scripted workflows. can wrap function small batch script process many melatonin profiles, save full result objects later inspection, export diagnostic plots, write compact summary results table one row per input file. idea works whether iterate file paths data frames already read R. code shows one example file-based workflow:
code: files <- list.files("path/to/profiles", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)  output_dir <- "dlmo_batch_output" plot_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "plots") object_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "objects")  dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create(object_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)  dlmo_results <- lapply(files, function(file_path) {   profile_name <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file_path))    result <- calculate_dlmo(     file_path = file_path,     threshold = 5   )    ggplot2::ggsave(     filename = file.path(plot_dir, paste0(profile_name, "_coarse.png")),     plot = result$dlmoplotcoarse,     width = 8,     height = 5,     dpi = 300   )    ggplot2::ggsave(     filename = file.path(plot_dir, paste0(profile_name, "_fine.png")),     plot = result$dlmoplotfine,     width = 8,     height = 5,     dpi = 300   )    saveRDS(     result,     file = file.path(object_dir, paste0(profile_name, "_dlmo_result.rds"))   )    result })  names(dlmo_results) <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(files))  summary_table <- data.frame(   file_name = basename(files),   profile_name = names(dlmo_results),   threshold = vapply(dlmo_results, function(x) x$threshold, numeric(1)),   interval_limit = vapply(dlmo_results, function(x) as.character(x$interval_limit), character(1)),   dlmo_coarse = vapply(dlmo_results, function(x) as.character(x$dlmo$coarse$time), character(1)),   dlmo_fine = vapply(dlmo_results, function(x) as.character(x$dlmo$fine$time), character(1)) )  writexl::write_xlsx(   summary_table,   path = file.path(output_dir, "dlmo_summary.xlsx") )  saveRDS(   dlmo_results,   file = file.path(output_dir, "dlmo_results_all_profiles.rds") )

Windows-based executable algorithm previously released (Danilenko & Verevkin, 2020), closed-source format limits flexibility. original software allow modification inspection underlying algorithm, lacks API integration analytical workflows, requires manual operation, making batch processing inefficient. bringing method R-programming environment, dlmoR provides open-source, transparent, scriptable alternative. enables reproducible batchable DLMO estimation, allowing users efficiently analyze multiple melatonin time-series within high-throughput workflows.

title: dlmoR 0.2.0
text: Single-point -threshold excursions treated blips ignored. Multi-point candidate rises compared using interval_limit. Later candidate rises within interval_limit can replace earlier candidates. Later candidate rises outside interval_limit replace earlier selected rise. Updated numeric interval_limit handling fractional hour values, 0.5, work documented. Added threshold interval_limit object returned calculate_dlmo(). Improved handling sparse poorly matched profiles giving informative errors fitting points remain.
